issues: Source coverage (upstream, unresolved by this review): the task grades only the Amanda/Morpheus branch, but the preparation plan's artifact inventory and export code identify five terminal scientific results from the converted notebook. `xtandem_filtered_psms.csv` (X!Tandem PSMs passing 1% FDR, `ftf` from `tandem.filter_df`, 1110 rows with a computed `q` column, byte-stable across replays per reference observations) and `msgf_filtered_psms.json` (MS-GF+ records passing 1% FDR, `msgf` from `mzid.filter`, byte-stable) are independent terminal scientific results of the same character as the in-scope `morph_filt`/`amanda_filt`, not diagnostic or preparatory outputs.

The stated exclusion reasons for those branches ('display diagnostics', 'XML/JSON representation-bound dumps', plot-only downstream consumption) are not valid reasons under the coverage policy: an ftf analog table is a tabular CSV terminal result, and nested JSON serialization / inconvenient parsing is explicitly not a reason to discard an independent scientific result.

Restoring the omitted endpoints requires different task construction — the supplied inputs are currently only `example.PSMs.tsv` and `example_output.csv`; `example.t.xml` and `example.mzid` are not materialized, and no reference outputs or grader checks exist for those artifacts. Adding grader checks to this candidate cannot recover the omitted branches, so the candidate is blocked rather than approved as a smaller task. See source_coverage for the full audit.

Grader-side review items (verified, for the record when the task is re-scoped): (a) the `shared_peptide_representatives` repair correctly implements the public per-peptide minimal-stratum rule — candidate sets are derived from the two declared reference PSM tables, keyed by `Sequence`/`Base Peptide Sequence`, minimal `Weighted Probability`/`Q-Value (%)`, values from a single PSM, matching both the instruction's tie rule and addendum check 10; the `shared-tie-representative-alt` valid-alternative control now passes and the wrong-solution probes still fail; (b) the re-annotated `amanda-row-swapped` probe is factually correct — the substituted PSM is found inside the submission copy of the reference table, so it is a retained row; the mutation duplicates one retained row and drops another, so `amanda_accepted_psm_rows` fails while `amanda_tda_qvalues`/`amanda_decoy_annotation` legitimately pass (q multiset and all-False isDecoy are unchanged); the script and overall reject outcome are unchanged, and the executed report confirms exactly this check-level pattern; (c) all 27 executed controls (reference, empty, recomputed, alternative, 3 missing-file, 20 probes of which 16 wrong_solution / 3 valid_alternative / 1 mixed-Pass) behaved as intended on this candidate hash; prior failed records for the earlier candidate are preserved per policy.

Minor gaps worth carrying into re-execution (non-blocking): no probe exercises a corruption of the Amanda-side representative pair (only Morpheus-side representatives were mutated) or a value placed exactly at the 1e-9 relative-tolerance boundary (the sub-tolerance control sits ~4.6e-16, far inside); `shared_peptide_representatives` fails wholesale ('not comparable') when membership fails — conservative over-rejection only, consistent with contract.
rationale: The grader itself is well implemented: the repaired tie-representation rule now matches the public contract (any single-PSM-consistent representative from the per-peptide minimal stratum, derived from the reference PSM tables rather than pinned to the reference's tie choice), the corrected amanda-row-swapped annotation is accurate against the actual edit, the comparator's typing/tolerance rules match the disclosed addendum (numeric iff every non-empty reference value parses finite; purely relative 1e-9 tolerance so zeros are exact; non-finite and unparseable numeric cells rejected; full-row multisets with exact counts), identities and cross-file relations are correct (Spectrum Number unique for Morpheus, full-row multiset for Amanda since Title repeats, one row per shared peptide, exact-string peptide keys, literal 'False' isDecoy, empty Scan Number held empty), and all 27 executed controls on this candidate hash behaved as intended, including the previously failed shared-tie-representative-alt now passing and the three valid-alternative controls passing (row reordering, sub-tolerance representation, alternative tie representative). However, the source coverage audit fails: the original notebook's terminal scientific results comprise five exported artifacts, and the task deliberately grades only the three Amanda/Morpheus artifacts, excluding the X!Tandem 1% FDR filtered PSM table (ftf, 1110 rows with computed q values) and the MS-GF+ 1% FDR filtered records (msgf) solely because they live in XML inputs and JSON/nested serialization. Those are independent terminal scientific results named in the preparation plan's artifact inventory, not diagnostic or preparatory outputs, and a plot being the only downstream consumer or inconvenient serialization is not a valid reason to discard them. Restoring these endpoints requires different task construction (supplying example.t.xml and example.mzid as inputs, new reference outputs, and new checks), which cannot be recovered by revising this grader; per policy the candidate is blocked rather than approved as a smaller task.
